faq-q1: Where is Dr. Kareem Zaher’s clinic located?
faq-a1: Our urology and andrology clinic is conveniently located in Zahraa El Maadi, Cairo, specifically in the 13th Sector at El Nada Tower (1st Floor). We serve patients from across Maadi, Cairo, and surrounding governates seeking specialized urinary and male reproductive care.
faq-q2: What is the best treatment for kidney stones?
faq-a2: The best treatment depends on the size and location of the stone. Dr. Kareem Zaher specializes in minimally invasive solutions, including Laser Lithotripsy and Endoscopic removal. These modern techniques allow for faster recovery and less pain compared to traditional open surgeries. We assess each case individually to recommend the safest path.
faq-q3: Do you treat Erectile Dysfunction (ED) and male infertility?
faq-a3: Yes. As a specialized Andrologist, Dr. Kareem provides comprehensive care for men's health issues. This includes the diagnosis and treatment of Erectile Dysfunction (ED), premature ejaculation, and Male Infertility (such as Varicocele surgery). We also offer advanced options like penile implants for severe cases.
faq-q4: What are the options for treating an enlarged prostate (BPH)?
faq-a4: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) is common in men as they age. We offer a range of treatments from medication management to endoscopic prostate surgery (TURP) and laser vaporization. Our goal is to improve urinary flow and quality of life with minimal side effects.
faq-q5: Do I need a referral to book an appointment?
faq-a5: No referral is necessary. You can book an appointment directly through our website or by calling our clinic in Maadi. We strive to offer flexible evening clinic hours (7:00 PM – 10:00 PM) to accommodate your work schedule.

et-p1: The 15-question International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF) Questionnaire is a validated, multi dimensional, self-administered investigation that has been found useful in the clinical assessment of erectile dysfunction and treatment outcomes in clinical trials.
et-p2: A score of 0-5 is awarded to each of the 15 questions that examine the 4 main domains of male sexual function: erectile function, orgasmic function, sexual desire and intercourse satisfaction.
et-p4: IIEF assessment is limited by the superficial assessment of psychosexual background and the very limited assessment of partner relationship, both important factors in the presentation of male sexual dysfunction.
et-p5: Analysis of the questionnaire should, therefore, be viewed as an adjunct to, rather than a substitute for, a detailed sexual history and examination.
et-p8: The international index of erectile function (IIEF): a multidimensional scale for assessment of erectile dysfunction.

vp-subtitle: Microscopic Subinguinal Varicocelectomy — the safest technique to protect fertility with fast, complication-free recovery.
vp-metric1-desc: The highest improvement rates in semen quality
vp-metric2-desc: Nearly non-existent compared to traditional surgery (15%)
vp-compare-sub: The essential clinical differences that guarantee your complete safety
vp-adv1-title: Complete preservation of the testicular artery
vp-adv1-body: The microscope provides precise magnification of up to 20–25×, allowing full visual distinction between the pulsating testicular artery and the surrounding enlarged veins, avoiding accidental ligation and protecting the testicular tissue from atrophy.
vp-adv2-body: In traditional surgery, lymphatic vessels are tied at random, causing fluid accumulation around the testicle in up to 7% of cases. Under the microscope they are fully preserved, reducing the rate to less than 0.4%.
vp-adv3-title: Ligation of all microscopic collateral veins
vp-adv3-body: Small collateral veins cannot be seen with the naked eye and are the main cause of varicocele recurrence. Seeing them clearly ensures the problem is removed at its root.
vp-benefits-sub: When does Dr. Kareem Zaher recommend microscopic surgery?
vp-ben1-body: Reducing warm blood pooling restores the testicle's natural temperature, improving sperm count, increasing motility, and reducing abnormalities and DNA fragmentation.
vp-ben2-body: Eliminating the annoying pulling or heaviness caused by venous blood stasis after long periods of standing or physical activity.
vp-ben3-body: Protecting the Leydig cells responsible for testosterone secretion from gradual damage, enhancing a man's vitality, physical and sexual performance.
vp-journey-label: The patient journey in the clinic and hospital
vp-timeline-title: Procedure steps and fast recovery period
vp-step1-body: The procedure is performed under supported local, spinal, or very light general anesthesia based on the patient's preference and medical assessment.
vp-step2-body: A very small cosmetic incision below the belt line (subinguinal) with no cutting of the abdominal wall muscles, closed with a completely hidden cosmetic suture.
vp-step3-body: The patient rests in the recovery room, has a light meal, and leaves the hospital walking normally the same day.
vp-step4-body: Return to office work and driving after two to three days, while avoiding heavy lifting and strenuous sports for 3 weeks.
vp-postop1: Wear a scrotal support (jockstrap) for two weeks to reduce tension and mild swelling.
vp-postop2: Showering is allowed after 48 hours using the sterile waterproof dressing on the wound.
vp-postop3: Perform a semen analysis for follow-up and assessment 3 months after the operation (the sperm production cycle).
vp-faq1-q: When does improvement appear in the semen analysis after surgery?
vp-faq1-a: The complete sperm production cycle in the testicle takes about 72 to 90 days. Therefore the first follow-up semen analysis is performed after a full 3 months, with cumulative improvement in motility and count continuing up to 6-9 months after surgery.
vp-faq2-q: Can a varicocele return after microscopic surgery?
vp-faq2-a: Microscopic surgery has the world's lowest recurrence rate at less than 1%, compared to 15% in traditional open surgery, thanks to the superior magnification that ensures all tiny feeding veins are ligated without exception.
vp-faq3-q: Does the procedure or the varicocele affect sexual ability and erection?
vp-faq3-a: The varicocele itself does not cause direct sexual weakness, but it may reduce testosterone production. Performing the surgery under the microscope fully protects the erection nerves and restores regular male hormone secretion with no negative effect on erection.

ll-title: Laser Lithotripsy of Kidney & Ureteral Stones with Flexible Scopes
ll-subtitle: Holmium Laser (Ho:YAG) — the safest flexible endoscopic technique for fragmenting stones and clearing the urinary tract with no surgical incisions.
ll-feat1-body: Advanced Holmium:YAG laser fibers fragment even the hardest calcium and uric acid stones into fine dust particles that are easily and spontaneously passed with urine without ureteral obstruction.
ll-feat2-body: The precision flexible ureteroscope can bend up to 270° to access and fragment stones lodged in the lower renal calyces with no external incisions.
ll-feat3-title: Superior Kidney Tissue Protection & Maximum Safety
ll-feat3-body: Laser lithotripsy offers exceptional precision that preserves the integrity of the ureteral wall and renal pelvis, with minimal bleeding compared to older surgical approaches.
ll-cand-title: Who Are Candidates for This Technique?
ll-cand-sub: Flexible ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy is the European gold standard recommended for the following cases:
ll-cand1: Ureteral stones causing acute renal colic attacks
ll-cand2: Kidney stones (single or branched) up to 2 cm in size
ll-cand3: Failure of previous Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy (ESWL)
ll-cand4: Patients on anticoagulants or those wishing to return to work and normal activity quickly
ll-step1-body: Low-radiation non-contrast helical CT scan to accurately determine stone location, hardness, and size in millimeters.
ll-step2-body: Performed under light general or spinal anesthesia, using high-definition digital imaging and Holmium:YAG laser pulses to completely fragment the stone.
ll-step3-body: Just two hours of recovery, then return home the same day. Resume normal daily activities within 24-48 hours with adequate hydration.

ll-book-desc: Comprehensive evaluation with low-radiation CT scan to determine the optimal laser lithotripsy plan for your case.

ll-faq-title: Frequently Asked Questions About Laser Lithotripsy
ll-faq1-q: Does the patient feel any pain during or after stone fragmentation?
ll-faq1-a: The procedure is performed under appropriate anesthesia to ensure complete pain relief throughout. After surgery, patients may experience mild, temporary burning during urination for the first 24 hours, which is easily controlled with prescribed pain medication.
ll-faq2-q: Is a ureteral stent required after the procedure?
ll-faq2-a: In some cases, depending on stone location, a fine temporary ureteral stent may be placed to ensure smooth urine flow and prevent renal colic after fragmentation. It is easily removed in the clinic after 1-2 weeks.
ll-faq3-q: When can I return to work and normal life?
ll-faq3-a: Most patients can resume their daily routine and light office work the next day, or within 48 hours at most, since there are no external surgical incisions.

tp-title: Endoscopic Prostate Enlargement Treatment with Tissue Vaporization
tp-subtitle: Bipolar TURP — a modern technique to restore normal urine flow without open surgery, while fully protecting urinary control and sexual function.
tp-sym1-body: Difficulty and slowness in starting urination, with frequent interruption into weak separate spurts.
tp-sym2-body: Waking up more than 3 times during the night, causing insomnia and chronic fatigue.
tp-sym3-body: A persistent sensation of not fully emptying the bladder after urination.
tp-sym4-body: A sudden urge to urinate immediately with an inability to postpone it.
tp-when-sub: Dr. Kareem Zaher's precise criteria for intervention
tp-when1: Symptoms not responding to conventional medication and its effectiveness declining.
tp-when2: Recurrent acute urinary retention requiring an emergency catheter.
tp-when3: Formation of bladder stones or impaired kidney function due to urine reflux.
tp-when4: Recurrent urinary bleeding or chronic microbial urinary tract infections.
tp-tech-title: The latest endoscopic technologies at the clinic
tp-tech1-body: Using normal saline instead of old solutions completely prevents TUR Syndrome, providing 100% safety for patients with heart disease and high blood pressure.
tp-tech1-note: Simultaneous instant vessel coagulation prevents bleeding
tp-tech2-title: Enucleation & vaporization of the enlarged lobe
tp-tech2-body: Complete cavity clearance while keeping the outer capsule intact, ensuring the enlargement does not return in the long term, with maximal widening of the urinary passage.
tp-tech2-note: Protecting the nerves responsible for erection and urinary control
tp-step1-body: Urinary tract ultrasound to measure prostate size and residual urine, plus uroflowmetry to precisely determine the surgical plan.
tp-step2-body: A safe operation lasting 45 to 60 minutes under light spinal anesthesia through the natural urethral opening with no incisions.
tp-step3-body: Removal of the urinary catheter within just 24-48 hours, and leaving the hospital with smooth urine flow and immediate comfort.
tp-rev1-text: "I used to wake up 5 times every night with severe difficulty. After plasma endoscopy with Dr. Kareem Zaher, thank God the catheter was removed the next day and I returned to my normal life and peaceful sleep."
tp-rev2-text: "The doctor's clear explanation and scientific honesty removed all my worry about the operation and its effect on sexual function. The procedure was smooth with virtually no pain."
tp-faq-title: Frequently asked questions about prostate enlargement
tp-faq1-q: Does the procedure affect urinary control?
tp-faq1-a: No. Only the enlarged tissue inside the prostate capsule is removed, staying completely away from the external urinary sphincter, thus preserving normal control at 100%.
tp-faq2-q: Can the procedure be performed on heart patients or those on blood thinners?
tp-faq2-a: Yes. Bipolar plasma technology features instant coagulation of blood vessels and no fluid absorption, making it the safest option for the elderly and those taking blood thinners, after medical coordination.
tp-faq3-q: When can I return to work and normal activity?
tp-faq3-a: The patient can walk on the same day of the operation and return to light office activities within 3 to 5 days after catheter removal, while avoiding heavy lifting for two to three weeks.

pp-cand1-desc: When there is no response to oral medications, stimulants or local injections.
pp-cand2-desc: Difficulty maintaining rigidity due to rapid venous blood leakage.
pp-cand3-desc: Severe curvature accompanied by erectile weakness and tissue fibrosis.
pp-cand4-desc: Damage to the neurovascular supply after major surgical interventions.
pp-road-title: Treatment and Recovery Journey Step by Step
pp-step1-body: Performing a color Doppler examination, measuring the tissue dimensions with extreme precision and choosing the ideal size customized for each patient.
pp-step2-title: Precise Surgery Through a Cosmetic Incision
pp-step2-body: A procedure lasting no more than 50 minutes through a tiny cosmetic incision (less than 2 cm), completely hidden and with the highest international sterilization standards.
pp-step3-body: Returning home on the same day, with the ability to resume normal daily activity and light work within just 48 hours.
pp-step4-body: A confidential training session to activate and use the implant, and to begin normal, successful marital relations after 4 to 6 weeks.
pp-rev1-text: "I suffered for long years with diabetes and tried every medication in vain. After the operation with Dr. Kareem, my self-confidence returned completely, the result is natural and impressive, and no one noticed anything."

pp-faq1-q: Does the implant affect sensation, orgasm or fertility?
pp-faq1-a: Not at all; the implant is placed inside the cavernous bodies responsible for rigidity only, while the external sensory nerves, the urethra, and the ability to feel and ejaculate remain 100% intact with no negative effect.
pp-faq2-q: Can a partner or anyone notice the implant?
pp-faq2-a: It can never be noticed; the implant is fully embedded inside the body under the skin and natural tissues, and the surgical incision is tiny and completely hidden with a concealed cosmetic suture.
pp-faq3-q: What is the lifespan of the implant and the warranty provided?
pp-faq3-a: The patient receives an international warranty card registered with a certified serial number for life from the leading American and European manufacturers, and it is designed to continue with full efficiency for a lifetime.

pc-subtitle: The latest radical solution to fragment and extract large and branched stones through a microscopic puncture not exceeding 5 mm, with the highest levels of safety.
pc-stat1-desc: Stone-Free Rate from the first session
pc-stat2-desc: Instead of the traditional 20 cm incision
pc-stat3-desc: Fast recovery and safe discharge the next day
pc-stat4-desc: Maximum protection of both kidney functions
pc-what-body: Mini-PCNL is the safest medical leap in modern urological surgery; an extremely thin nephroscope is inserted through an opening not exceeding 4 to 5 millimeters in the back to reach the kidney cavity directly under precise interventional imaging, allowing the fragmentation of extremely hard stones with a hydraulic laser or mechanical waves and their immediate suction without the need for an open surgical incision.
pc-what1: Suitable for large stones (larger than 2 cm) and complex staghorn stones.
pc-what2: Complete avoidance of the severe bleeding associated with traditional open surgeries.
pc-what3: Negligible post-operative pain with a cosmetic scar that gradually disappears.
pc-cmp-sub: Why do doctors prefer Mini-PCNL for large stones?
pc-cmp2-label: Recovery period and return to work
pc-cmp3-label: Complete clearance rate of the large stone
pc-cand1-desc: Those exceeding 1.5 cm to 2 cm in diameter, which are difficult to pass naturally through the ureter.
pc-cand2-desc: Complex stones like antlers that fill the renal pelvis and branch inside the kidney calyces.
pc-cand3-desc: Hard, highly dense stones that resisted extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) or flexible ureteroscopy.
pc-cand4-title: Narrow calyceal neck or kidney abnormalities
pc-cand4-desc: Patients suffering from a localized obstruction that prevents the fragments from flowing out automatically.
pc-step1-body: Performing a spiral CT scan (3D CT Urography) to determine the precise location of the stone and plan the safest access route without touching vital blood vessels.
pc-step2-body: Under comfortable general anesthesia, a microscopic puncture is made and the stone is fragmented with a precise laser, and all fragments are completely extracted under direct vision on 4K screens.
pc-step3-body: Performing an ultrasound examination to confirm complete kidney clearance, then removing the small tube and discharging the patient within just 24 hours in excellent health.
pc-step4-title: Return to Normal Life and Sustainable Prevention
pc-step4-body: Resuming daily tasks and office work within a few days, with a customized dietary and medical protocol to prevent the future formation of stones.
pc-review-chip: A patient treated at the clinic
pc-rev1-text: "I suffered from a 3.5 cm staghorn stone, and all the doctors agreed on a painful abdominal or back open surgery. Thanks to God and then the skill of Dr. Kareem Zaher, he performed the Mini-PCNL through a very small puncture for me, and I left the hospital the next day with no noticeable pain, and the scan showed the stone had completely disappeared."
pc-faq1-q: Does the procedure leave any noticeable scar?
pc-faq1-a: The surgical puncture is extremely small (about 4-5 mm only) and is closed with a fine cosmetic suture or a special medical adhesive strip, making the mark almost non-existent and it fades completely over time.
pc-faq2-q: Does the endoscope affect the efficiency or function of the healthy kidney?
pc-faq2-a: On the contrary, the Mini-PCNL technique was designed specifically for maximum preservation of kidney tissue (Nephron Sparing), as the endoscope is guided through a safe anatomical path that does not touch the vital renal blood vessels.
pc-faq3-q: When can I return to driving and working?
pc-faq3-a: Most patients can resume driving and light office activities within 48 to 72 hours of leaving the hospital, while avoiding heavy lifting for only two weeks.

tb-chip-tech: Advanced & Precise Urologic Tumor Surgery · TURBT
tb-subtitle: Accurate diagnosis and radical resection of bladder tumors and wall through the natural urethra with no surgical incision, along with immediate pathological examination of the safety margins.
tb-doctor-cred: Consultant of Urology and Andrology • MSc In Urology • Member of the European Association of Urology (EAU)
tb-stat1-desc: Complete resection through the natural passage
tb-stat2-desc: Safe En-Bloc resection of the base
tb-stat4-desc: Accurate determination of tumor depth and grade
tb-what-title: What is the TURBT technique and advanced endoscopy?
tb-what-body: TURBT is the global Gold Standard for diagnosing and treating superficial and invasive bladder tumors; a fine endoscope equipped with an electrical resection loop or bipolar plasma (Bipolar Loop) is inserted to remove the growing tissue and coagulate the feeding vessels with extreme precision and virtually no bleeding.
tb-what1-desc: Complete removal of the tumor tissue down to the muscle layer to ensure clean safety margins and prevent residual cells.
tb-what2-desc: Absolute bleeding control using normal physiological saline, which avoids fluid absorption syndrome and its risks.
tb-what3-desc: The possibility of injecting a preventive local dose into the bladder cavity immediately after the endoscopy to prevent future tumor recurrence.
tb-sym-title: Indications for Bladder Tumor Resection Endoscopy
tb-sym1-desc: Blood or blood streaks in the urine without burning or severe colic, which is the most common and important first sign.
tb-sym2-title: Masses or thickening in the bladder wall
tb-sym2-desc: Detecting polyps or abnormal irregularity in the bladder lining via ultrasound or contrast-enhanced CT.
tb-sym3-title: Frequent urinary urgency resistant to treatment
tb-sym3-desc: A persistent and sudden urge to urinate or burning that does not respond to antibiotics for urinary tract infections.
tb-sym4-desc: A scheduled surveillance examination for patients who had a previous tumor resection to confirm the wall is completely healthy.
tb-road-title: Treatment and Recovery Journey Step by Step
tb-step1-body: Ultrasound, urine cytology analysis, and prior medical coordination with the anesthesia consultant and routine blood tests.
tb-step2-body: Gentle painless spinal or general anesthesia; the tumor is removed and its base resected with extreme precision under advanced visual magnification within 30 to 45 minutes.
tb-step3-body: Placing a gentle urinary irrigation catheter for 24-48 hours to ensure clear urine and bladder comfort, followed by its removal and a successful hospital discharge.
tb-step4-body: Discussing the detailed tissue result with Dr. Kareem Zaher to determine the periodic protection strategy or the need for periodic preventive instillation.
tb-rev1-text: "I consulted Dr. Kareem after sudden blood in my urine, and through immediate examination an early superficial tumor was discovered and removed endoscopically with no surgery or noticeable pain. I left the hospital the next day and the result was completely reassuring, and the clinic team follows up with me periodically with full honesty."
tb-faq-title: Frequently Asked Questions about Bladder Tumor Resection Endoscopy
tb-faq1-q: Does the procedure cause any pain or wounds in the abdomen?
tb-faq1-a: There is no external wound or openings in the abdomen at all; the procedure is performed entirely through the natural urethra with the latest fine endoscopes under full anesthesia to ensure complete patient comfort.
tb-faq2-q: When does the analysis result of the removed tumor sample appear?
tb-faq2-a: The precise pathology result appears within 5 to 7 working days; through it, the cell type, grade, and depth of invasion into the bladder wall are determined to set the most suitable preventive treatment plan.
tb-faq3-q: When can the patient resume work and normal life?
tb-faq3-a: The patient can return to light work and normal life within 3 to 5 days after removing the urinary catheter, with the recommendation to drink 2 to 3 liters of water daily and avoid strenuous physical exertion for two weeks.
